Bangladesh Commerce Bank Limited, the respondent No.1 herein, filed the above suit for realization of Tk.43,87.797.00 by sale of the mortgaged properties stating, inter alia, that Bangladesh Commerce and Investment Limited, in the course of their banking business sanctioned loan of Tk. 25,00,000/-to the defendant No. 1, the petitioner No.1 herein, and as security for the above loan the defendant No.1 deposited Tk. I0,00,000/-and the defendant No.9 mortgaged her immovable properties situated at Purana Paltan Line Dhaka and the defendant No. 10 became guarantor for the loan and the defendants also executed several documents and the defendants having failed to repay the loan notices were issued to the defendants on 1.3.1992 claiming payment of Tk.21,39,049.00 which was then overdue; as per decision of Bangladesh Bank, by Public Notice dated 28.4.1992 the activities of Bangladesh Commerce and Investment Limited remained suspended and as a result they could not take any further steps against the defendants for realization of the ousting loan amount then by Act 12 of 1997 the respondent No.1 was constituted wherein all the assets and liabilities of the erstwhile Bangladesh Commerce and Investment Limited vested; then the respondent No. 1 by various letters requested the defendants to make payment of the outstanding dues but with no result and hence the suit. The defendants contested the above suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that late Sheikh Abdul Hye, the then Managing Director of the defendant No. 1, was an illiterate and simple man; Bangladesh Commerce and Investment Limited though not a bank, induced late Sheikh Abdul Hye to make a deposit of Tk. 10.00,000/- for availing loan facilities and being induced he deposited Tk. 10.00,000/-with Bangladesh Commerce and Investment limited against sanction of loan of Tk. 25,00,000/- to the defendant No. 1 and he did not authorize the Bangladesh Commerce and Investment Limited to encase the above amount of Tk. 10,00,000/- which was to be kept as fixed deposit; Late Sheikh Abdul Hye withdraw only an amount of Tk. 13,00,000/- lacs from the sanctioned amount of Tk. 25,00,000.00 and on different dates he also repaid the same but the dishonest officers of the Bangladesh Commerce and Investment Limited/respondent No. 1, taking advantage of his illiteracy and simplicity, did not adjust the amount deposited and misappropriated those deposits; further without any notice and authority the respondent No. 1 also encased the above fixed deposit of Tk. 10,00.000/- and also illegally showed that an amount of Tk.22,74,225.00 was due from the defendant No. 1 as On 30.4.2001; if the account of the defendant No.1 is audited by an expert it will be revealed that the defendant No. 1 has paid to the respondent No. 1 more than the amount due; the claim of the respondent No. 1 is also barred by limitation; Bangladesh Commerce and Investment Limited not being a bank or financial institution functioned like a commercial bank without any licence; further the name of Bangladesh Commerce and Investment Limited not being in the list of the banks or financial institutions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 the Artha Rin Adalat has no jurisdiction to entertain and try the present suit and the suit ought to have been instituted in an ordinary civil court. Thereafter on 26.9.2004 the defendants filed an application under Order 7 Rule 10 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for return of the plaint to the respondent No. 1 for filing the same to proper court. The respondent No. 1 opposed the above application by filing written objection. The learned Joint District Judge, after hearing, rejected the above application holding that the respondent No. 1 was established by Act No.12 of 1997 as a commercial bank and that the defendant No. 1 took loan from its predecessor, a financial institution, and as such the Artha Rin Adalat has jurisdiction to try the suit. The defendants then moved the High Court Division whereupon a Rule was issued in Civil Revision No.6558 of 2002 and, after hearing, the High Court Division discharged the Rule.
